facts.value: The source-visible runtime storage includes a 96-record HSD_SM pool, a 64-entry synth-instance mapping, a two-by-sixteen send-default matrix, and paired AXFX contexts. Initialization clears only each record's SMSTATE_MASK bits and inserts it into the free list. Logical sound creation installs a command stream and channel defaults; successful pending-start processing installs the synth-to-record mapping. Channel send changes attempt updates to matching records subject to the external-override gate and always store the default for valid indices. Auxiliary setup copies caller settings into the selected persistent effect context and registers that context on successful initialization.
facts.rationale: Corrects whole-record clearing, mapping-producer attribution, and unconditional send-propagation claims without asserting compiled layout.

evidence.why: Conditional record updates and persistent defaults.

facts.value: Source-declared uninitialized driver globals begin zeroed. Initialization inserts all 96 records into the free list and resets the AXFX arena, but does not explicitly reset the active-list head, generation, clock, or voice counters; repeatable reinitialization is not established. Sound creation assigns a generation-qualified handle, inserts an active record, and increments the logical-record count. Clock updates recycle state-zero records and decrement that count. The metadata loader clears its completion flag before the asynchronous read; its callback sets the flag only when result != -1, so a -1 result alone does not release the callback-pumped wait.
facts.rationale: Separates initial static state from explicit reset operations and preserves the exceptional DVD result.

facts.value: Requests pause for the singleton path-selected stream's retained synth handle. Returns false when the slot is -1; otherwise forwards the handle to HSD_SynthSFXPause and returns true without checking whether the synth node still exists. It preserves the retained handle and does not pause all pooled sound effects.
facts.rationale: Replaces a liveness guarantee with the actual sentinel-only request semantics.

evidence.why: Missing synth node is a no-op.

facts.value: Requests resume for the singleton path-selected stream's retained synth handle. Returns false only when the slot is -1; otherwise forwards the handle and returns true, even if the synth lookup finds no node or the node is already unpaused. The wrapper preserves the retained handle.
facts.rationale: The Boolean result reports forwarding, not active-instance availability or a completed transition.

facts.value: Commits pending operations in one HSD_SM record: starts synth playback, forwards priority, volume, pan-control, two pitch-ratio and main/Aux A/Aux B mix updates, or transitions the record to sleep or key-off retirement. Pending bit 0x10 has no synth action. Bit 0x200 invokes the shared retirement helper, not a record callback.
facts.rationale: Corrects the callback interpretation using the actual helper body.

facts.value: Scans pending bits 0 through 9 in ascending order and clears each normally completed bit. Successful start records the returned synth handle, installs its mapping, clears start-related flags and increments the mapped-instance count. Failed start asserts active state, clears SMSTATE_MASK and returns. Bit 0x100 replaces the masked state with SMSTATE_SLEEP and returns. Bit 0x200 calls shared key-off retirement and returns. These exceptional paths bypass the normal per-bit clearing statement and stop later operations in that invocation.
facts.rationale: Preserves the ordering and early-return distinctions while replacing nonexistent callback dispatch with retirement.

evidence.why: Ordering, success, failure and terminal branches.

facts.value: Returns -1 for the implemented bank/sample upper-bound failures, a track outside 0–255, a channel outside 0–15, a paused channel, or an empty free list. It does not explicitly reject negative sound IDs, negative bank indices or negative resolved sample indices, so these guards are not complete malformed-ID validation. On success it reserves a record, resets its synth ID, schedule and flags, installs controls and the command stream, constructs a generation-qualified handle, and under interrupt protection marks it active, inserts it at AXDriver_804D7794 and increments AXDriver_804D77D0.
facts.rationale: Corrects the claim that every invalid bank or member is safely rejected.

facts.value: Provides externally controlled per-sound auxiliary-send routing. When the selected bus's external-override bit is set, it changes that sound's Aux A or Aux B send and, for an assigned synth instance, recomputes coupled direct/Aux A/Aux B gains. This permission is independent of whether an AXFX processor is installed on the bus; processor selection is stored in separate configuration nibbles.
facts.rationale: Distinguishes external command override from effect enable state.

facts.value: Rejects negative or out-of-pool logical handles, bus indices outside 0–1, a clear selected external-override bit, stale handles, and records with zero masked state. The selected gate is bit 0 for Aux A or bit 1 for Aux B in AXDriver_804D603C, not the effect-type field. Under interrupt protection, an assigned synth instance receives the stored send-byte change and recalculated mix immediately; a record with vID == -1 must be active, stores the byte and sets 0x80000 without a synth call. Both accepted paths restore interrupts and return true.
facts.rationale: Retains exact branches while correcting the meaning of the gate.

facts.value: The channel argument filters state-bearing records by itdflag. Each match supplies its logical handle to AXDriver_8038D5B4 together with the selected bus and send_level cast to u8. That helper may reject the request, including when the external-override gate is clear; its return is ignored. After traversal, the raw eight-bit level is stored in AXDriver_804C5A20[aux_bus][channel], which later sound creation copies into HSD_SM.x24.
facts.rationale: Corrects unconditional propagation while preserving the current/future data paths.

evidence.why: Inner rejection, ignored result and default write.

facts.value: Provides channel-scoped auxiliary-send control for one of sixteen logical sound channels. It saves the selected Aux A or Aux B default for future sound records and attempts to update current matching records. Current records adopt the change only when the per-sound setter accepts it, so an override-disabled channel/bus combination can retain a new future default without changing current sounds.
facts.rationale: Separates guaranteed default storage from conditional current-sound updates.

evidence.why: Conditional current updates and unconditional valid default.

facts.rationale: Meaningfully improves the rendered SetAuxLevelAll hypothesis by exposing the required channel filter and channel-default update. This remains a behavioral inference, not a recovered historical spelling.

evidence.why: Channel validation, filtering and indexed default.

facts.value: Sets the saved send-level default for one auxiliary bus on one logical sound channel and attempts to apply that level to every current state-bearing record on the channel. Existing-record updates use the gated per-sound setter; future records inherit the saved default.
facts.rationale: Removes the unsupported guarantee that every existing record is updated.

facts.value: Returns false without mutation for channel indices outside 0–15 or bus indices outside 0–1. Valid indices enter an interrupt-disabled traversal, attempt a per-sound send update for each matching state-bearing record, then replace the saved default, restore interrupts and return true. Inner failures are ignored. A clear external-override bit can prevent current-record updates while the new default is still retained; this is independent of the installed effect type.
facts.rationale: Preserves the outer success semantics while correcting the bus-enable interpretation.

evidence.why: Exact guards, ignored failures and default transition.

facts.value: A parameterless int(void) accessor returning AXDriver_804D77C8, the count of driver-mapped synth instances. The lookup has 64 slots, but this is not a count of individual AX hardware voices: successful instance creation increments once even when the synth node owns two voices. Explicit key-off can remove the instance from this count before hardware teardown completes.
facts.rationale: Corrects the physical-voice count interpretation while preserving the exact accessor signature and diagnostic terminology.

evidence.why: One or two AX voices owned by a synth node.
